# Continual-ARC vertical object repacking

## Observed task pattern
In one verified task family, the input contains several separated nonzero shapes. The output preserves each shape's cells, color, orientation, and horizontal (column) position, but translates whole shapes vertically. Objects end up packed against the top or bottom edge, with vertical gaps removed within their destination group. The assignment of a given object to the top vs. bottom is not safely inferred from initial height alone; use the demonstration pairs to identify the assignment rule.

## Workflow
1. Segment the grid into distinct nonzero objects (usually 4-neighbor connected components; check whether same-colored adjacent pieces merge).
2. Record each object's color, bounding box, exact local bitmap, and column offset.
3. Compare demos: match objects by bitmap/color and note whether each is moved to the top or bottom; verify rigid translation and unchanged columns.
4. Infer the top/bottom assignment rule only from repeated evidence. Do not assume objects simply stay near their original vertical half.
5. Reconstruct the output by translating each object's bitmap without rotation/reflection. Pack top-assigned objects upward and bottom-assigned objects downward, preserving horizontal placement and any demonstrated ordering/spacing constraints.
6. Check the full grid dimensions and ensure no overlap; fill all other cells with 0.

## Verified example
A solved 16x15 instance had five objects: a 3x3 color-3 ring and a 4x4 color-1 ring moved to the top; a 3x4 color-1 ring moved to the top below the larger ring; a color-8 asymmetric 4x3 shape and a color-2 4x5 shape moved to the bottom. Every object retained its bitmap, orientation, and columns. This demonstrates vertical rigid translations and edge packing, but the top/bottom assignment rule requires task-specific demo analysis.
